title: Atomic Optimize config commit with webhook handshake and SDK retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a transactional commit flow for Optimize automation config changes that guarantees either a verified commit or a safe rollback. The flow will offer an API and SDK primitives to submit a proposed config, perform a webhook-driven verification handshake with target services (runtime, console, dedicated controllers), and finalize commit or rollback based on verifications and policy. Goal: eliminate half-applied states from automated recommendations, provide clear retry semantics, and enable safe canary rollforwards.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /optimize/commits creates a commit record and returns a commit_token; subsequent retrying the exact same payload returns the same token (dedup semantics)
API: POST /optimize/commits/{commit_token}/verify triggers webhook deliveries and returns a verification status; failures mark commit as 'verification_failed'
SDK: SDK helpers expose commit(), verify(), finalize(commit_token, action) with retry/backoff that are idempotent across client crashes
Rollback: finalize(commit_token, 'rollback') must produce a deterministic revert and emit rollback-event to audit log
Canary: support staged 'rollforward' to X% of routes with automatic health checks and automatic rollback on regression signals
Observability: each stage emits structured events (commit/verify/success/rollback) visible in Console timelines and Grafana alerts
Safety: if verification webhooks do not respond within the configured timeout, commit state becomes 'verification_timed_out' and no partial changes remain applied in runtime
technical_notes: Use optimistic commit_token (UUID + request_hash) stored in commit-store with TTL; tokens are stable for identical payloads to support client retries
Webhook handshake: deliver signed HTTP POST to registered verifier endpoints with HMAC; expect 200/202 acceptance and an async callback to /_webhook/callback with verification result
Two-phase apply: runtime controllers receive an 'apply-intent' and only perform local dry-run + health-checks; final 'apply' is sent once verification succeeds

Conflict resolution: commits that touch overlapping targets use a lightweight lock with compare-and-swap (version vector) to decide serialization; conflicting commits auto-enqueue and surface to Console
Canary orchestration: orchestrator will apply to a percentage of traffic and run SLO probes (latency, error rate, cost delta) for configured interval; regression triggers rollback
Idempotency: avoid global transactions; achieve atomicity via orchestrated steps + compensating rollback and explicit commit states
Telemetry: include correlation_id in all webhook calls and SDK operations for traceability
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff - design reviewed with PM and Runtime leads. Agreed on token-based dedup rather than write locks to improve client UX.
2026-02-26: Prototype - webhook endpoint and callback handler implemented in optimize-controlplane (branch: feat/commit-handshake). Basic end-to-end local test passes for single verifier.
2026-03-02: Design feedback from Security - require HMAC signing + replay window; adjusted webhook payload schema and added timestamp nonce.
2026-03-05: SDK design - JS/Go SDK proposal posted. Decided SDK expose high-level commitUntilVerified helper that retries verification and emits structured events.
2026-03-09: Integration tests - canary orchestration test against mocked runtime shows expected rollback on induced latency regression. Working on adding audit events.
2026-03-10: Blocker discovered - race when two commits target same cache shard causes both to progress to 'applied' in worst-case; investigating locking strategy and compensating rollback sequence.
comments: Priya Menon (2026-02-24): Make sure we include a human-readable summary in audit logs for enterprise compliance.
Ethan Browne (2026-03-03): Can we reuse the existing rollout engine for canary steps? If so, capture its error signals instead of reimplementing probes.
Nadia Romero (2026-03-08): Security approves HMAC approach but requests an optional mTLS mode for on-prem verifiers.

Marco Li (2026-03-10): Working on a CAS-based shard lock change; if we can't converge this sprint we'll ship verification-first path that blocks concurrent shard changes and surfaces manual resolution.
